blocks.text: CITY OF ILAGAN—The province of Isabela was placed in a state of calamity after a prolonged drought caused P2.881 billion in agricultural losses, mostly in corn and rice farms, since July. The provincial board unanimously approved, on Nov. 12, a resolution sponsored by board member Evyn Jay Diaz, chair of the committee on disaster management, declaring a state of calamity. Gov. Rodolfo Albano III concurred with the measure, which was made public on Monday. The provincial agriculture office reported the losses based on consolidated data submitted by municipal agriculture offices through the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Information System Corn farms […]...
